definitions.explanation: To write something down clearly and explicitly so there is no ambiguity. Used in formal, legal, and business contexts for information that must be recorded precisely.

examples.japanese: {住所|じゅうしょ}と{氏名|しめい}を{明記|めいき}してください。
examples.english: Please clearly write your address and name.

examples.japanese: {契約書|けいやくしょ}には{条件|じょうけん}が{明記|めいき}されている。
examples.english: The conditions are clearly stated in the contract.

examples.japanese: {応募|おうぼ}の{際|さい}は{希望|きぼう}{職種|しょくしゅ}を{明記|めいき}の{上|うえ}、{履歴書|りれきしょ}を{送付|そうふ}してください。
examples.english: When applying, please send your resume with the desired position clearly noted.

notes:
USAGE:
Used as a suru verb ({明記|めいき}する) or noun. Very common in instructions on forms, contracts, and official documents. The pattern {明記|めいき}の{上|うえ} means 'having clearly stated' and is standard in application instructions.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ～を{明記|めいき}する: to clearly state ~
- {明記|めいき}の{上|うえ}: having clearly noted (on documents)
- ～に{明記|めいき}されている: is clearly stated in ~

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {明示|めいじ}: explicit indication (showing clearly, not necessarily in writing)
- {記載|きさい}: entry, description (writing down, less emphasis on clarity)
